translationRepairs: At the beginning of Yong'an in Wei, his second elder brother Hui was betrothed to Liang; he memorialized that Xi be released from commoner status and made attendant cavalier, and Xi was summoned to serve as recorder on the staff of Prince of Guangping's opening office.

At the beginning of Yong'an in Wei, his second elder brother Hui went on mission to Liang; he memorialized that Xi be released from commoner status and made attendant cavalier, and Xi was summoned to serve as recorder on the staff of Prince of Guangping's opening office.
In s0059, 第二兄暉聘梁 is an envoy posting to Liang, not a betrothal; 'was betrothed to Liang' misreads 聘 and invents a marriage alliance with a state.

When the prince reached Ye, Yang Yin, Murong Yan and others were executed; an edict made him grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.

When the prince reached Ye, Yang, Yan and others were executed; an edict made him grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.
Chinese has only 誅楊、燕等; 'Murong Yan' invents a surname absent from the unit, and reducing to 'Yang, Yan and others' matches the source abbreviations.
Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi pat his chest with his hand and withdrew.
Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi patted his chest with his hand and withdrew.
Narrative past tense requires 'patted' for 拊胸; the literal's 'pat' is an English verb-form error, and the proposed fix matches the Chinese action.
